Hi Mina — thanks, and great to hear Acme is ready to progress. Attached is a first-pass draft with a pricing staircase and notes on channel flow (spreadsheet stub attached). High-level summary below.

Attachment: 20261113-jb-private-offer-draft.xlsx (stub)

Proposed pricing staircase (high level):
- Band A: 0 - 100k tokens/mo — list rate, no discount (intended for baseline usage)
- Band B: 100k - 500k tokens/mo — 15% off list at commit threshold
- Band C: 500k - 1.25M tokens/mo — 25% off list once committed volume hit
- Band D: >1.25M tokens/mo — 35% off list (volume accelerator)

Channel & marketplace assumptions:
- Standard reseller commission we plan for: 12% of Redwood net (pre-marketplace fees) as a starting point.
- AWS marketplace fee typically ~5% (varies by arrangement) — this is applied on gross/list in some cases; we can structure the private offer so fees are applied to Redwood list price and then commissions are calculated on the net we invoice.
- Two common patterns we see: 1) Redwood invoices Acme directly and pays reseller commission on net revenue; 2) Marketplace invoices Acme and passes payment, with reseller commission handled as a separate payment from Redwood to reseller. Pattern (1) gives clearer revenue recognition for Acme and Redwood; pattern (2) is faster for some resellers.

Open items for Acme to confirm:
- Do you want MedBridge to be the billing party on AWS (marketplace pass-through) or prefer Redwood to invoice Acme directly?
- Any PO or payment timing constraints (net30 vs net45)? I saw terms in the RFP but want to confirm.

Ben/Laura — tagging you to pull margin impact and confirm whether the 12% reseller baseline + 5% marketplace fee keeps us within acceptable net rev thresholds for a starter deal.

If that looks reasonable I'll set up a 30-min alignment call next week with Mina + MedBridge + Amy (AWS) to lock the structural choice.

Thanks,

Jordan / Laura — ran the numbers quickly against the staircase Jordan proposed. Attached is a compact margin calc. Notes below:

Attachment: channel_margin_calc_v3.xlsx (stub)

Quick math (assume list price $0.012/token — placeholder for modeling):
- Band B (100k-500k, 15% off): effective price = $0.0102/token
  - Marketplace fee (5% of list) = $0.0006/token
  - Reseller commission (12% on our net) =~ $0.001224/token
  - Redwood net ≈ $0.008376/token (after fees & commission)
- Band C (25% off): effective price = $0.009/token; Redwood net ≈ $0.00705/token after same fee structure
- Band D (35% off): effective price = $0.0078/token; Redwood net ≈ $0.00599/token

Implications:
- For the starter commitment window (expected first 3 months ~200k tokens/mo), gross to Redwood net delta is ~17-20% after fees and reseller commission. That is acceptable short-term if we secure committed ARR and a 12–18 month ramp to target; not acceptable if ACME expects immediate break-even in month 1.
- If MedBridge insists on being paid by AWS marketplace (pass-through), our accounting is slightly more complex but operationally doable. If they want Redwood to handle commission payouts (Redwood -> MedBridge), we prefer that from a revenue recognition and invoicing simplicity perspective.

Recommendation:
- Offer the Band B/Band C staircase as proposed, cap initial trial credits to avoid heavy negative margin in month 1, and require a minimum committed monthly usage for the first 6 months to protect economics.

I'll be on the alignment call if scheduled.
